newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa testing the water on fx controls - Stals.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa testing the water on fx controls - Stals.

text.p: The South African government aimed to test demand for the withdrawal of funds from the country by gradually relaxing capital restrictions, Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Thursday.
"We are moving gradually to test reaction all the time," he told a roadshow of financial market participants.
Asked what kind of pent-up demand there was to take funds offshore, Stals said it was difficult to assess.
"We know there is something in the region of 600 billion rand -- 10 percent of 600 billion rand would not be unreasonable," he said.

Stals said earlier this week that the next step in the gradual easing of exchange controls could include private individuals for the first time, but he stressed that any moves would not be spectacular.
Finance Minister Trevor Manuel, addressing the same meeting, said only that talks were continuing on the matter.
"As is obvious, there is a lot of work in progress in this area," he said.
Many financial analysts expect Manuel to make an announcement on foreign exchange controls in or around his March 12 budget.
